questions.question: The Scrum artifact containing work selected for the current Sprint.
questions.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is the set of Product Backlog items selected for the Sprint, plus a plan for delivering them.

questions.question: The metric in Agile that measures team productivity based on completed work.
questions.explanation: Velocity measures how much work a team completes in a Sprint, typically in story points or hours.

questions.question: The Agile practice of writing automated tests before writing production code.
questions.explanation: TDD is a practice where developers write failing tests first, then write code to make the tests pass.

questions.question: The acceptance criteria technique using Given-When-Then format.
questions.explanation: BDD uses scenarios written in Given-When-Then format to specify expected behavior in business terms.

questions.question: The practice of merging code changes frequently into a shared repository.
questions.explanation: Continuous Integration involves regularly merging code changes and running automated builds and tests.

questions.question: The Kanban metric measuring average time from work-started to done.
questions.explanation: Cycle Time measures how long it takes to complete a work item from start to finish.

questions.question: The Agile principle of maintaining a sustainable pace of work indefinitely.
questions.explanation: Sustainable pace means the team works at a consistent speed that can be maintained long-term without burnout.

questions.question: The Extreme Programming practice of refactoring code to improve design continuously.
questions.explanation: Continuous refactoring improves code structure incrementally without changing external behavior.

questions.question: The definition that determines when a user story is considered complete.
questions.explanation: Definition of Done is the shared understanding of what it means for work to be complete and releasable.

questions.question: The Kanban policy limiting the number of items in each workflow stage.
questions.explanation: WIP limits constrain how many items can be in each column, helping identify bottlenecks and improve flow.

questions.question: The time-boxed research activity used to investigate uncertain technical questions before estimating work.
questions.explanation: A spike is a short, time-boxed investigation or prototype used to reduce uncertainty so a story can be estimated.

questions.question: The shared checklist of criteria a backlog item must satisfy before it can be pulled into a Sprint.
questions.explanation: Definition of Ready ensures a story is clear, estimated, and sized correctly before the team commits to it in Sprint Planning.

questions.question: The consensus-based estimation technique where team members reveal numbered cards simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Planning Poker has each member privately choose an estimate card and reveal at once, avoiding anchoring bias.

questions.question: A large body of work too big for one Sprint, later broken down into multiple user stories.
questions.explanation: An epic is a large user story or feature set that must be split into smaller stories before it can be delivered in a Sprint.

questions.question: The Lean software development principle of removing all activities that add no customer value.
questions.explanation: Lean identifies waste such as partially done work, extra features, and task switching, then systematically removes it.
